Here’s a straightforward sheet-pan plan using the boneless chicken breasts, potatoes, onions, and carrots you mentioned. It’s forgiving and easy to tweak.

Sheet-pan lemon-garlic chicken with potatoes and onions (serves 2–4, depending on portions)
- Ingredients
  - 2 boneless, skinless chicken breasts
  - 2–3 potatoes, cut into 1-inch chunks
  - 1 large onion, cut into wedges
  - 1–2 carrots, sliced (optional)
  - 2–3 tablespoons olive oil
  - Salt and pepper
  - 1 teaspoon garlic powder (or 2 minced garlic cloves)
  - 1 teaspoon paprika or Italian seasoning (optional)
  - Lemon wedges for finishing (optional)

- Timing and temperature
  - Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
  - Bake about 25–30 minutes. The chicken should reach 165°F (74°C) in the thickest part; potatoes should be tender when pierced with a fork.

- Step-by-step
  1) Line a sheet pan with parchment for easy cleanup (optional).
  2) Cut potatoes and onions (and carrots if using) into roughly 1-inch pieces.
  3) Toss potatoes/onions/carrots with 1–2 tablespoons olive oil, salt, pepper, garlic powder (or minced garlic), and paprika/Italian seasoning if you like. Spread in a single layer on the pan.
  4) Pat the chicken dry with a paper towel. Season with a little salt and pepper; place on the sheet pan with the vegetables.
  5) Drizzle the remaining olive oil over the chicken. If you have lemon, tuck a few lemon wedges under the chicken or lay a slice on top for bright flavor.
  6) Bake 25–30 minutes. Check that the chicken is 165°F inside and the potatoes are tender.
  7) Let rest 3–5 minutes, then squeeze a bit of lemon juice over the dish if you have it, and serve.

- Quick tips
  - If your potatoes are a bit larger, give them a head start by par-cooking them for 5–7 minutes in boiling water (or 3–4 minutes in the microwave) before tossing with the chicken on the sheet. This helps finish together.
  - If you’re using very thick chicken breasts, you can butterfly them (slice in half horizontally) to reduce cooking time and help them stay juicy.
  - You can swap in any sturdy veggie you like (peppers, green beans, brussels sprouts) as long as you cut them to similar sizes.
